frames.title: Right now — AI tools, and this crash site
frames.body: College by day, building AI-flavored tools by night. This portfolio is the current proof: a debugger that crashed on purpose, with a RAG brain that answers questions from my real GitHub data — entirely in your browser.

frames.title: Building for myself — the phase tutorials can't teach
frames.body: Stopped following tutorials and started making small tools I personally needed. Learned the two lessons that stick: shipping is a skill, and deployment is a feature — not an afterthought.

frames.title: CS fundamentals — and falling down the AI rabbit hole
frames.body: Tech major, deep in data structures and systems. Then LLMs happened: prompting, embeddings, retrieval, agents. What started as curiosity became the thing I build toward every week.

frames.title: The first line of code — audience of one
frames.body: Teenage me, wanting an app that didn't exist, realizing nobody was going to build it for me. The first script was clumsy and mine. That's still the whole philosophy: build it for yourself, learn it for real.
